newsitem.title: USA: Cobalt industry response mixed on Stockpile bids.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt industry response mixed on Stockpile bids.

text.p: Cobalt industry executives had mixed responses Thursday to a "draft solicitation" proposed by the U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center (the Stockpile) at an industry meeting in Virginia.
But most agreed that the new proposal took several steps towards taking out ambiguities in the original solicitation.
The meeting comes in the wake of a legal challenge to the Stockpile's last "negotiated solicitation" for cobalt by Minor Metals Inc's, in which the U.S. District Court ruled against Minor Metals Inc.

"The solicitation takes several steps in the right direction," said a cobalt trader who requested anonymity, "but it still doesn't take away the fact that there is no transparency in the negotiated sales."
The new solicitation establishes evaluation factors that specify the basis for formula pricing, payment terms, and removal schedules.
In the previous negotiated sale all such terms were subject to negotiation.

One large cobalt consumer supported the new format of "negotiated bids" being adopted by the Stockpile, saying that "these bids are the only way a large consumer can assure himself a long term supply of cobalt supplementary to our normal supply channels."
One trader with a large European based trading house also supported the "negotiated bid" because it kept the terms of the bid completely confidential.
"We would certainly be less willing to participate if the sealed bids were the only method of buying cobalt from the government," he said.

In general smaller traders preferred the original format of "sealed bids", in which all terms were constant except the bid price, because in the words of one trader, "its the only way of establishing any transparency in this market."
Lacking any exchange-based trading, Stockpile "sealed bid" sales are the only transparent forum for pricing cobalt, traders said.
In the new format of "negotiated bids", only a rough estimate of total value and quantities sold are given by the Stockpile.
The latest Stockpile proposal calls for the sale of 1.5 million pounds of cobalt. The deadline for bids is August 29.
